newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Capitall sees earnings rise "over time".
newsitem.headline: Capitall sees earnings rise "over time".

text.p: South Africa's Capital Alliance Holdings Ltd, part of the black empowerment consortium that bought mining house JCI Ltd earlier this year, said a substantial earnings rise could be expected "over time".
The mining-to-financials group said in a statement accompanying year end results that the opportunities for organic growth, acquisitive expansion and value extraction continued.

"Across the group results for the year are extremely encouraging both in terms of achieved earnings and increased capacity, and shareholders should expect significant real increases in earnings over time," said chairman Mzi Khumalo.
Capitall earlier posted a surge in earnings for the year to end-March to 102.4 cents a share before exceptional items, up from 52.9 cents a year ago.
It posted a dividend of 15.0 cents from 10.0 previously.
The past year was an acquisitive period for Capitall which bought businesses including a banking operation, a stockbroking firm, investment house and a property firm.
"Each acquisition has been made in terms of a sound long-term strategy which will position Capitall as one of the leading players in the country's financial services sector," Khumalo said.
